programs.name: Science-Based Minimalist Workout Plan (Under 45 Mins)
programs.author: Jeff Nippard
programs.summary: Two short full-body sessions a week, each under 45 minutes, using 1-2 very hard sets per exercise with drop sets, myo-reps and a superset to save time. The author also explains how to spread the same two workouts over 3, 4 or 5 days.
programs.evidenceNote: Direct weekly volume is low, about 3-5 hard sets per major muscle (chest about 4, quads about 3, hamstrings about 3 plus drop sets), which is below the roughly 10+ weekly sets linked to the most growth in dose-response studies but enough for good progress or maintenance when sets go to or near failure. It suits people short on time. Its weak points are that it depends on true failure and good technique on single sets, and the free version gives no progression or deload rule.

programs.schedule: 2 days per week: Full Body Day 1 and Full Body Day 2, run on separate days. Author's other options: 3 days = Full Body 1 + Day 2 split into an upper and a lower day; 4 days = split both full-body days into upper/lower (upper, lower, rest, upper, lower, rest); 5 days = upper/lower plus push/pull/legs. Sets and reps stay the same, and you may add sets or weak-point exercises on the split days.

progression.description: The free video and blog give no formal progression scheme. The method is quality over quantity: take each single set to failure (or within 1 rep of failure) with perfect technique, then use the stated drop sets or myo-reps. A heavy strength set (4-6) comes before a lighter back-off set (8-10) on the dumbbell press and hack squat. The author gives no load increments, so incrementKg is null.
progression.deload: Not specified in the free video or blog.

programs.notes: Uses the jeffnippard.com blog (the written version of the 2022 video) as the source of record. Warm up with 2-3 minutes of brisk walking plus arm and leg swings. The paid 12-week Essentials Program is built on these workouts but is out of scope. Level is a judgement call: the author calls the paid Essentials version suitable for all levels, but the free plan relies on training to failure.

days.name: Full Body Day 1
days.focus: Full body (chest, hamstrings, back, quads/glutes, triceps, side delts, calves)

exercises.name: Flat Dumbbell Press (heavy set)
exercises.notes: Strength set first. Lower with the elbows tucked 30-45 degrees, flare on the press if comfortable.

exercises.name: Flat Dumbbell Press (back-off set)
exercises.notes: Lighter hypertrophy back-off set.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Push the hips back and let the dumbbells drop straight down until you feel a big hamstring stretch. Use straps if grip limits you.

exercises.name: 2-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.notes: Set 1 overhand middle grip, set 2 underhand close grip. Optionally strip the weight after set 2 for overhead cable curls.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
exercises.notes: Per leg, one leg at a time. Go to failure or within 1 rep of it, with the front leg doing all the work. Use straps.

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
exercises.notes: To failure, then drop the weight 30-40% and go to failure again.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
exercises.notes: To failure, then drop 30-40% and go to failure again. Cable or dumbbell lateral raises work if there is no machine. Stopping at 90 degrees is fine.

exercises.name: Leg Press Toe-Press
exercises.notes: Straight-leg calf raise on the leg press. Pause about 1 s at the bottom and squeeze at the top. To failure, then drop 30-40% and go to failure again without bouncing.

days.name: Full Body Day 2
days.focus: Full body (quads, chest/shoulders, back, hamstrings, biceps, abs)

exercises.name: Hack Squat (heavy set)
exercises.notes: 2-3 warm-up sets. Top set at about RPE 9 (1 rep shy of failure), then rest about 3 min. Full depth, and the knees may travel past the toes.

exercises.name: Hack Squat (back-off set)
exercises.notes: Lighter weight, control the negative and focus on the quads.

exercises.name: High-Incline Smith Machine Press (superset A1)
exercises.notes: Bench at 45-60 degrees, slightly closer grip. Superset with the T-bar row, resting 30-60 s between the two exercises if needed.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row (superset A2)
exercises.notes: One set with a wide grip, one with a close grip. Substitute: chest-supported incline dumbbell row, same sets and reps.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.notes: Lean forward for more stretch. To failure, then drop 30-40% and go to failure again.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Biceps Curl
exercises.notes: To failure, then myo-reps with the same weight: rest 3-4 s, do 4 reps, and repeat until you can no longer get 4.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch (rope, kneeling)
exercises.notes: To failure, drop 30% and go to failure, then drop another 20-30% and go to failure one last time. Let the whole spine round.

programs.name: The Ultimate Push Pull Legs Series (2023, free YouTube version)
programs.author: Jeff Nippard
programs.summary: A six-day bodybuilding-focused push/pull/legs week that Nippard published free as a six-video YouTube series in 2023, with each muscle trained twice a week. The powerlifts get only one hard top set a week plus back-off work, and most sets are taken close to or to failure, with techniques like feeder sets, lengthened partials and inter-set stretching.
programs.evidenceNote: Each muscle is trained twice a week for roughly 10-15 hard sets (for example chest about 11, quads about 12), many at RPE 9-10, which fits current hypertrophy evidence for intermediates. Strength work is deliberately minimal (one top set per lift per week), so it is not a strength program. Some techniques, such as inter-set stretching, stretch-only partials and the 'press-around', rest on early or limited evidence, as the author himself says. Six days a week is a heavy time commitment.

programs.schedule: Six sessions in playlist order: Push 1, Pull 1, Legs 1, Push 2, Pull 2, Legs 2. The free videos do not say where rest days go. The author says these workouts make up Phase 1 (first 6 weeks) of his paid program, which also comes in 4- and 5-day versions that are not published free.

progression.description: Stated per exercise, with no single global rule. Top sets (squat 1x2-4 at 85-90% 1RM, RPE 8-9; bench 1x3-5 with about 1 rep left; deadlift 1x5 at RPE 8-9) are followed by back-off sets loaded off the top set (paused squat about 75%, Larsen press about 75%, stiff-legged deadlift about 50-60%). For load-focused lifts (EZ-bar curl, floor skull crusher, decline crunch) track weight and reps and add one or the other week to week. Pull-up AMRAP: match or beat last week's reps, adding at least 1 rep a week when cutting. Optional deadlift linear periodization: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 reps over weeks 1-5 while adding weight each week. Hypertrophy-only lifters can keep the deadlift at 5 reps and add weight or improve technique. The author gives no kg or lb increments, so incrementKg is null.
progression.deload: Not specified for the free 6-session week. In the optional deadlift linear periodization, week 6 is a deload: 4 reps at a lighter load. The author says the paid 12-week program ends with a full deload week, but that program is out of scope.

programs.notes: Source of record: Push 1 and Pull 1 from Nippard's own blog posts (the written versions of those videos); Legs 1, Push 2, Pull 2 and Legs 2 from the video audio via caption transcripts. The playlist order and Legs 2's closing line ('that's a wrap for the six part push-pull leg series') confirm that the six videos form one week. Only the free Phase 1 week is represented: the paid Ultimate Push Pull Legs System (Phases 2-3, spreadsheet, 4- and 5-day versions) is out of scope. The author does not state session length, so sessionMinutes is an estimate. Warm-up each day: 5-10 min on a treadmill or StairMaster plus dynamic stretches, then a warm-up pyramid before the heavy compound lifts.

days.name: Push 1
days.focus: Chest, shoulders, triceps (bench strength top set)

exercises.name: Bench Press (top set)
exercises.notes: Single max-effort top set after a warm-up pyramid: bar speed should slow and you could maybe get 1 more rep. Substitute a flat dumbbell or machine press with the same sets and reps.

exercises.name: Larsen Press
exercises.notes: Bench press with the legs up and no leg drive, at about 75% of the top-set weight. Slightly closer grip, 1-2 s down and 1-2 s up.

exercises.name: Standing Arnold Press
exercises.notes: Load progressively like an overhead press: squeeze the glutes and drive through the heels. A belt and straps help.

exercises.name: Press-Around (+ pec stretch)
exercises.notes: One-arm cable press past the midline. After each arm's set, hold a static pec stretch on that side for 30 s at about 7/10 intensity, then switch.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Cable Y-Raise
exercises.notes: Start with the cable across the body, like drawing a sword, and raise out and back on a diagonal. Do not turn it into a front raise.

exercises.name: Squeeze-Only Pressdown (superset A1)
exercises.notes: Bottom-half partials (the lockout part only). Go straight into the stretch-only overhead extension with no rest.

exercises.name: Stretch-Only Overhead Extension (superset A2)
exercises.notes: First-half partials in the stretched position only.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Triceps Extension
exercises.notes: Cable extension with the arm across the body, for triceps work at a different shoulder angle.

days.name: Pull 1
days.focus: Lats, upper back, rear delts, biceps

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown (feeder sets + 2 failure sets)
exercises.notes: First do 3 feeder sets of 10 at about RPE 4-5, 6-7 and 7-8 (resting 1-2 min). Then 1 set of 10 to failure, rest 2-3 min, and a second failure set with the same weight (usually 7-8 reps), then strip about 30% for a mini drop set of 4-5 reps. Middle grip, straps or a thumbless grip.

exercises.name: Omni-Grip Chest-Supported Row
exercises.notes: Set 1 wide grip, set 2 slightly closer grip, set 3 neutral or underhand grip.

exercises.name: Bottom-Half DB Pullover (+ static lat stretch)
exercises.notes: After each set, stretch each lat for 30 s (swap which side goes first on set 2), then rest 30 s.

exercises.name: Omni-Direction Face Pull
exercises.notes: Set 1 cable low, pulling low to high; set 2 at shoulder height; set 3 high, pulling down toward the eyes.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Biceps Curl
exercises.notes: Heavy. Track the numbers and add weight or reps each week.

exercises.name: Bottom-Half DB Preacher Curl
exercises.notes: Stretched-position partials, one arm at a time: weaker arm first, then match the reps with the stronger arm.

days.name: Legs 1
days.focus: Quads, hamstrings, glutes, calves, abs (squat strength top set)

exercises.name: Squat (top set)
exercises.notes: After a 4-5 set warm-up pyramid, one set at 85-90% 1RM, about RPE 8-9. Hypertrophy-only option: hack squat (first choice) or Bulgarian split squat (second) for 4-6 reps.

exercises.name: Paused Squat (back-off)
exercises.notes: About 75% of the top-set weight, with a 1-2 s pause in the hole and an explosive drive up.

exercises.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Keep the bar tight to the legs and reverse at about knee to mid-shin. Cut the top 10-25% for more hamstring focus.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
exercises.notes: 10 per leg (20 strides). Knee touches the floor, control the negative, and use straps so grip does not limit the load.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.notes: Optional toe positions: out on set 1, in on set 2, straight on set 3. Lean forward to feel the stretch.

exercises.name: Leg Press Toe Press
exercises.notes: Optional: toes out on set 1, in on set 2, straight on sets 3-4.

exercises.name: Decline Plate Crunch
exercises.notes: Round the lower back and squeeze the abs. Add weight or a rep from session to session.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Barbell Incline Bench Press
exercises.notes: Undulating sets: a moderate set of 8, a heavier set of 5, then a light pump set of 15. Rest at least 3-4 min before the set of 5. Grip just outside shoulder width.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.notes: First 2 sets at about RPE 9, last set to failure. Arms below parallel, thumbless grip, constant tension.

exercises.name: Floor Reset Skull Crusher
exercises.notes: Strength-focused: the bar comes to a dead stop on the floor each rep. Track the numbers and add weight or reps each week.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Cable Pec Fly
exercises.notes: Hinge forward at the hips and fly straight out for stability.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
exercises.notes: First 5 reps with a slow 5 s eccentric, then 15 constant-tension reps (1 s up, 1 s down).

exercises.name: Plate Front Raise
exercises.notes: Turn the plate like a steering wheel (internal rotation) to bring in more side delt. Substitute a dumbbell Y-raise if it hurts.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
exercises.notes: One all-out AMRAP set to failure, with a controlled tempo.

days.name: Pull 2
days.focus: Lats, upper back, traps, rear delts, biceps

exercises.name: One-Arm Half-Kneeling Lat Pulldown
exercises.notes: Keep the forearm in line with the cable and stop at the midline.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.notes: One all-out AMRAP set. Each week match or beat last week's reps (add at least 1 when cutting). Grip about 1.5x shoulder width. Use a band or machine assistance if needed.

exercises.name: Kroc Row
exercises.notes: A looser dumbbell row with a more upright torso and controlled body English. Stricter form is fine if you prefer.

exercises.name: Cable Shrug-In
exercises.notes: Shrug up and in.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.notes: Sweep out and back. Optionally change grip each set: neutral, then pronated, then internally rotated.

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Biceps Curl
exercises.notes: Kneel and curl with the arm out to the side and overhead. You may add a couple of extra curl sets if you need more biceps volume.

days.name: Legs 2
days.focus: Posterior chain, quads, calves, abs (deadlift strength top set)

exercises.name: Deadlift (top set)
exercises.notes: One heavy top set at RPE 8-9 after a warm-up pyramid. Substitutes: trap bar deadlift, barbell hip thrust, or Bulgarian split squat.

exercises.name: Stiff-Legged Deadlift (back-off)
exercises.notes: About 50-60% of the top-set weight. Hips high, knees straighter. Start light and stay shy of failure until the technique is comfortable.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.notes: Medium stance, full depth, constant tension (no lockout). Rest no more than 2 min.

exercises.name: Glute Ham Raise
exercises.notes: Cut the top quarter. Substitute a counterweighted setup on a lat pulldown or Nordic ham curls.

exercises.name: Slow Eccentric Leg Extension
exercises.notes: 3 s eccentric on every rep.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.notes: Replacing it with standing calf raises is reasonable if there is no machine.

exercises.name: Roman Chair Leg Raise
exercises.notes: Go close to failure and curl the pelvis up. Bend the knees if you cannot get 10 straight-leg reps. Slow the negative to 2-3 s if 20 is easy.
